text:
arjun: Heads-up — product is asking for per-tenant runtime metrics for private/VPC installs (token usage, egress bytes, per-route latency) + audit hooks (KMS key_id, envelope ops). We need to coordinate agent handshake, firewall constraints, and what the console will show. Who wants to own the ingestion API?
talia: We planned to have the agent emit Prom-style metrics locally and push an envelope to the customer-configured collector. For Redwood-managed telemetry we do a signed push to our ingest endpoint. Question: push vs pull for on-prem customers?
mike: Firewall reality: many customers only allow outbound 443 and sometimes require TLS SNI to a pinned host. gRPC on 443 (with TLS) is ok, but non-443 ports get blocked. If we want long-lived connections we should multiplex over HTTPS.
nora: Security note: KMS usage must be auditable. Do NOT transmit plaintext keys or raw signatures. Metrics envelope should include key_id, operation type (encrypt/decrypt/sign), and a detached attestation token. Also want an audit-log hook configurable to forward to customer SIEM (syslog/HTTPS).
oleg: For Redwood Console dashboards we need a minimal ingestion schema so UX can rely on it: {tenant_id, route, timestamp, tokens_sent, tokens_generated, latency_ms, batch_size, fallback_count, routing_policy}. If we can't send full cardinality routing_policy, include a policy_hash so we can rollup.
sre-jen: From SRE side: agent should expose a /health and /metrics endpoint locally and support a forwarding mode that samples traces (no PII) to reduce bandwidth. Also need backpressure handling so we don't impact inference latency.
arjun: How about quotas? Product wants per-tenant soft quotas emitted as metrics and hard enforcement at the runtime layer. We need a label to map metrics to quota buckets.
talia: We can add a labels map on the envelope: route, policy_hash, quota_bucket. But cardinality risk — encourage using hashed IDs for high-cardinality fields. We'll need runtime change to attach policy_hash to requests earlier in pipeline.
mike: Network handshake idea: agent initiates TLS to ingest.redwood.example with mTLS cert (customer-kept) OR token-based client auth. If customer firewall only allows specific egress IPs, we must provide a small set of egress IPs or support customer NAT. Also support proxy env vars.
nora: KMS: we should support both customer-managed key (CMK) id in envelope and Redwood-verifiable HSM attestation. Audit hooks should include request_id to link metric -> key operation.
oleg: UX ask: For rollouts we want a per-canary dashboard split by routing_policy so product can watch quality and cost. If we only get policy_hash we can show buckets, but need to map hash->human name via a controlled lookup (sent separately over admin channel).
arjun: Can someone prototype a minimal handshake payload we can send to security and infra for review? We need the exact fields for firewall and SIEM teams.
talia: I mocked one up — small JSON envelope, pushing over HTTPS POST /v1/telemetry with Authorization: Bearer <agent-token>. We sign payload with customer key and include header X-Redwood-Agent: <version>. Example:
```
POST /v1/telemetry HTTP/1.1
Host: ingest.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <agent-token>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Agent: agent-0.9.1

{
  "tenant_id": "t-abc123",
  "ts": 1680000000,
  "metrics": [{"name":"tokens_generated","value":1234}],
  "labels": {"route":"/chat/generate","policy_hash":"p_h_9f2"},
  "kms": {"key_id":"arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd","op":"encrypt","attestation":"<b64sig>"},
  "audit_hook": {"syslog_forward":"tcp://siem.company:514"}
}
```
mike: That looks fine. Two asks: (1) support TLS SNI and Host header pinning, (2) allow customers to whitelist a small set of egress IPs or publish DNS names they can pin.
sre-jen: Also add a low-overhead retry/backoff and local queue size limit. If ingestion fails we should sample error traces and increment a metric we expose locally.
nora: I'll review the prototype for sensitive fields. We should redact or hash tenant identifiers in any telemetry sent to Redwood-managed ingest if customer requires.
oleg: Devex: once schema is stable we'll need a small docs page + example Grafana dashboard JSON. I can take the dashboard template if you assign me the final field names.
arjun: Ok — action items: talia to put prototype JSON in a PR, mike to list egress IPs/DNS options, nora to give KMS/audit checklist, oleg to draft dashboard template. I'll coordinate with product on quota semantics.
deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: telemetry-proto v0.1 -> staging at 2024-11-05T18:00Z :information_source: 
oleg: thanks — i'll start the dashboard draft and link it in the PR.
